slot.brief: Draw an ester structure (figure), treat with two equivalents of a Grignard reagent followed by acid workup, and ask which tertiary alcohol forms (distractors from single-addition products).

stem: The ester shown is treated with $2$ equivalents of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}$ followed by dilute $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$. Which product is formed?

verdicts.working: The ester is ethyl propanoate. Two equivalents of ethylmagnesium bromide add two ethyl groups to the carbonyl carbon; after hydrolysis, it bears three ethyl groups and OH, giving 3-ethylpentan-3-ol.

working:
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} \longrightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COC}_2\text{H}_5$
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COC}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{COH}$
Product: 3-ethylpentan-3-ol.

Independent check: The ester is ethyl propanoate. Two equivalents of ethylmagnesium bromide add two ethyl groups to the carbonyl carbon; after hydrolysis, it bears three ethyl groups and OH, giving 3-ethylpentan-3-ol.
solution:
An ester reacts with $2$ equivalents of a Grignard reagent to form a tertiary alcohol after hydrolysis; the alkoxy group is displaced during the first addition.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \xrightarrow[\text{then }\text{H}_3\text{O}^+]{2\,\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{MgBr}} (\text{C}_2\text{H}_5)_3\text{COH}$$
The product is 3-ethylpentan-3-ol.

figure.description: Draw the skeletal structure of ethyl propanoate: CH3CH2C(=O)OCH2CH3. Show the carbonyl oxygen double-bonded to the carbonyl carbon, and the –OCH2CH3 group single-bonded to that carbon.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Stops at the ketone formed after the first addition. B: Mistakes the ketone intermediate for an alcohol. D: Places the hydroxyl group at the wrong carbon.
